summary: Iteration 24 — Verified Tracy's COD pivot & CariPay/wallet removal. 12/13 backend tests PASS + all frontend acceptance checks PASS. One CRITICAL pre-existing bug surfaced: PUT /api/orders/{order_id}/status is wired to the WRONG function (helper `_status_timestamp_field` instead of `update_order_status`) so order status transitions silently no-op. This blocks the requested logistics-flow progression (confirmed → preparing/picked_up/delivered) after COD. Everything else (COD confirm, wallet/CariPay removal, WiPay button, /wallet redirect, Privacy/Terms, admin mail status) works as specified.

critical.issue: Decorator @api_router.put("/orders/{order_id}/status") at server.py:2250 is attached to the helper `_status_timestamp_field(status: str)` (line 2251) instead of the real `update_order_status(...)` defined at line 2381. Result: the endpoint returns 200 with body like "delivered_at" (the timestamp-field name) and NEVER touches MongoDB — order.status stays unchanged. Confirmed: after PUTs for preparing/picked_up/delivered all returning 200, GET shows status='confirmed'. This breaks the COD logistics-flow requirement.

minor.issue: Even once the decorator bug above is fixed, `_authorize_order_status_change` (server.py:2261) only allows user_type 'restaurant' or 'driver' — admin/agent are explicitly NOT allowed to update status. The current test seeded admin succeeded only because the route is no-op; once fixed, admins will receive 403. Recommend allowing user_type in ('admin','agent') OR add an admin override branch.

action_items: FIX server.py:2250 — move the `@api_router.put("/orders/{order_id}/status")` decorator down to directly above `update_order_status` at line 2381 (the helper `_status_timestamp_field` should NOT be a route). This is a one-line move and is BLOCKING the user-stated requirement that COD orders be able to progress through the logistics flow.
Update `_authorize_order_status_change` to permit admin/agent roles to update any order's status (currently only restaurant/driver, never admin).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2250 — route decorator misplaced one function above intended target. This is a textbook 'helper accidentally became a route' bug. After fixing, also add a unit test that PUT /api/orders/{id}/status actually mutates the document (Create → PUT → GET pattern).

/api/orders POST (server.py:2173) accepts the full Order model from the client and overwrites only customer_id server-side — clients can set financial fields (subtotal/delivery_fee/total/commission/etc.) and the server recomputes. Looks safe due to calculate_order_financials, but still requires `customer_id` in payload despite ignoring it (causes 422 if omitted). Consider switching to OrderCreate.

confirm_order_cod (server.py:2429) correctly: (a) auths the customer or admin, (b) blocks if already paid, (c) sets payment_method=cash/payment_status=cod_pending/status=confirmed, (d) best-effort driver assign, (e) fires WhatsApp notify in background. WhatsApp/Twilio mocked — no 500s observed.

rca_of_the_issue: Bug RCA — PUT /api/orders/{order_id}/status no-op: A FastAPI route decorator binds to whatever function immediately follows it (the next `def`/`async def`). In server.py, line 2250 has `@api_router.put('/orders/{order_id}/status')` and line 2251 begins `def _status_timestamp_field(status: str) -> Optional[str]:` — a 5-line dict-lookup helper. So FastAPI registered THAT helper as the route handler. The real `update_order_status` (line 2381) has no decorator and is therefore unreachable as an HTTP route. Reproduction: PUT /api/orders/{any-id}/status?status=delivered → 200 with JSON body `"delivered_at"` (the dict value the helper returns). Mitigation: move the decorator line 2250 down to be the line immediately above `async def update_order_status(...)` at line 2381 (and delete the orphaned decorator at 2250). Then add a Create→PUT→GET assertion test to prevent regression.
